# hyperlite_acl (Resource)

One assignment: a role given to an account or a group on one object. One resource per assignment, so several configurations can give rights on the same object without overwriting each other.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The group may create and run VMs in the pool...
resource "hyperlite_acl" "ops_on_web" {
  subject_type  = "group"
  subject       = hyperlite_group.ops.id
  role          = hyperlite_role.deployer.key
  resource_type = "pool"
  resource      = hyperlite_resource_pool.web.id
}

# ...and put their disks in this storage pool.
resource "hyperlite_acl" "ops_on_fast" {
  subject_type  = "group"
  subject       = hyperlite_group.ops.id
  role          = hyperlite_role.deployer.key
  resource_type = "storage"
  resource      = hyperlite_storage_pool.fast.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `resource` (String) The object: a VM's, container's, storage pool's or network's name, or a pool's id (`hyperlite_resource_pool.x.id`).
- `resource_type` (String) What it is given on: `vm`, `pool` (of VMs), `container`, `storage` (a storage pool) or `network`.
- `role` (String) A predefined role (`drive`, `operator`, `manager`) or a custom one (`hyperlite_role.x.key`).
- `subject` (String) The account's name, or the group's id (`hyperlite_group.x.id`).
- `subject_type` (String) `user` or `group`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The assignment's id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By its id.
terraform import hyperlite_acl.ops_on_web 12
```
